rules.description: No em dashes or en dashes anywhere, including ranges
rules.note: U+2012 figure dash and U+2015 horizontal bar included for completeness

rules.description: Hyphen used as a range or parenthetical dash (space-hyphen-space)
Curly quotes and apostrophes normalised to straight
Banned AI-tell words and phrases (case-insensitive, word-boundary)
banned_phrases: at the end of the day
notes: not only: bans the 'not only X but also Y' construction; verifier-approved clinical text never needs it
moreover/furthermore/additionally/overall/ultimately/notably/importantly/interestingly: banned as sentence openers; the trailing comma variants catch this
best practices: allowed only inside a direct quotation from a cited guideline title

excludes_architecture_title: the H1 is not scanned when it matches brief.title exactly. The architecture fixes page titles, so 0.5.5 'Meet the Researchers' trips the 'meet the' ban on a line no drafter is allowed to change. Prose that repeats the phrase in the body is still caught.

rules.description: Flag (do not fail) if any paragraph opens with a transition word
Rule-of-three rhythm: flag if more than 30 percent of sentences contain a three-item comma list
Sentence length variance too low (uniform rhythm is an AI tell)
US spellings banned
exceptions: verbatim journal titles, society names and cited paper titles in the reference list (reference list is excluded from UK-001 scope)
randomized/randomised: -ize forms permitted only inside reference list entries
acetaminophen: body text must use paracetamol

rules.description: Every in-text [n] marker has a matching reference entry and vice versa
No citation markers inside Junior or Patient tier body text (references live at article level; lower tiers stay clean)
No measurement, angle, dimension or normal range where the brief forbids figures (Section 0: entry requirements, test scores, fees)
notes: Page ids, section references and decision references are removed before the scan, because the prose on this site is full of them.
A bare small integer is allowed so a list can be numbered in prose. Any digit carrying a unit, a decimal point, or a value above ten is a quantity.
The reference list is outside the body scope, so a citation year never trips this rule.

rules.description: Every figure in the body is registered in the page's figure register with a claim and a verification state
notes: The client's instruction was to keep the measurements and check them. The build environment has no source access, so every figure is written from memory and none can be attributed to a paper. This rule does not judge a figure; it refuses an unregistered one, so the checking list cannot fall behind the pages.
A figure the reviewer deletes or corrects is marked REMOVED in the register rather than deleted from it, so the register is a record of what was checked.
Same extractor as FIG-001, so the two rules cannot disagree about what a figure is.

rules.description: Clinical recommendations on a professional page are registered for sign off
rules.applies_when: the brief requires any tier from medical_student upwards
notes: Warn rather than fail. The detector is a heuristic over imperative openers and directed modals, and a false positive must not be able to block a page. What it must do is surface drift between the pages and the list somebody is signing.
It over collects on purpose: a false positive costs a reviewer one line, a false negative leaves unsigned clinical advice on a professional page.
A sentence the reviewer judges to be teaching rather than clinical direction is marked NOT_CLINICAL in the register rather than deleted from it.

rules.description: A consultant block that frames a clinical decision names the five patient factors
rules.applies_when: the brief requires the consultant tier and the consultant block carries clinical direction
notes: Warn, for the same reason POS-001 warns: the detector is keyword matching over the block's text and a passing mention satisfies it. It surfaces an absent factor; it cannot certify a present one.
Scoped to a block that tells a clinician what to do. A consultant block about a teaching or departmental decision has no patient in it, and 3.1.7 is deliberately out of scope.
The factor list and its keywords live in the template, not here, so the rule and the editorial standard cannot drift apart.

rules.description: No fabricable bibliographic detail on a landmark papers page: an exact year, a journal, a volume or page number, a DOI, a PMID, or an et al citation form
rules.applies_when: the brief's page_type is one of page_types below

banned_shapes.exact_year: a four digit year that is not written as a decade
banned_shapes.volume_pages: a volume, issue or page range in the 12(3):456 or pp. 456 shape
banned_shapes.journal: a journal name or its abbreviation

notes: This is the rule that stands in for source access. The Operations Handbook grades an invented citation as its one critical failure, and the parts of a citation that get invented are the precise ones: the year, the journal, the volume and the page. A finding and the surname it is taught under are recalled together and are checkable from either; a volume number recalled alone is a guess that looks like a fact.
A decade is allowed, because the 1970s is the precision actually available and it says so. 1976 is not allowed, because it claims a precision this process does not have.
Scoped to landmark papers pages. Other pages carry real dates for real events, and 3.1.7 Historical Development is a page of them.

EV-40. The scope was hardcoded as landmark_papers inside linter.py while this file said nothing, so the rule's reach could not be read here. Same shape as the bug decision 028 fixed for ACC-001 and as the condition template's body_sections_rule before it. Moving it changes no behaviour. Widening it was measured and refused: the detector is a surname followed by a reporting verb, which is landmark papers prose, and across the rest of the site it returns almost only sentence initial words such as Postoperative, Extrusion, Whether and Choose. It does not find an eponym used as the name of a grading system, which is not an attribution of a study to an author and is not what the register holds.

rules.description: Every study attributed to a named author on a landmark papers page is in that page's attribution register
rules.applies_when: the brief's page_type is one of page_types below
notes: Warn, for the reason POS-001 and DEC-001 warn: detecting an attribution is keyword matching over a surname followed by a reporting verb, and it will both miss and over-read. It surfaces an unregistered attribution; it cannot certify that a registered one is right.
The register is what a reviewer with a library actually works through. Its value depends entirely on being generated from the pages rather than compiled by hand, which is why the rule exists at all.

rules.description: No bare diagnostic accuracy figure on an examination, imaging or reporting page: a sensitivity, specificity, predictive value or likelihood ratio written as a number
rules.applies_when: the brief's page_type is one of page_types below
notes: The same argument as ATTR-001, applied to a different fabricable quantity. For an examination test the comparative pattern is recalled robustly and is standard teaching: Lachman beats anterior drawer, the pivot shift is specific and insensitive, McMurray is specific and insensitive. A specific percentage is recalled alone, nothing in the pattern constrains it, and a wrong one looks exactly like a right one.
A wrong sensitivity is more dangerous than a wrong anatomical figure, because it changes what a clinician does next with a negative test. That is why this is a fail rather than a warn.

Angles, distances and grades are untouched. The flexion angle for a Lachman is part of the technique, is not a fabrication risk of this kind, and is registered as a figure under decision 006 like any other measurement.
The page says the comparison instead, which is what the evidence actually supports from memory, and the reviewer can add the figures once a source exists.

Extended to imaging pages by decision 028. 'MRI is 95% sensitive for a meniscal tear' is the same fabrication as a sensitivity for the McMurray test: the comparative standing of the modalities is standard teaching and recalled robustly, the percentage is recalled alone and nothing constrains it. The scope is this page_types list rather than a page type named in linter.py, because a rule whose scope lives in code cannot be read off the config, and this repository has already shipped one rule whose scope was prose that nothing read.

rules.description: Required blocks present per brief: tier blocks, key learning points, FAQs where required, reference list
Commercial terms banned when brief.governance.commercial_content_allowed is false
notes: excludes_architecture_title: the H1 is not scanned when it matches brief.title exactly, and the cross link labels are not scanned at all. The architecture names page 4.22.7 'Sportshealing Knee Score', so the rule as written banned that page's own title on its own page and banned the correct cross link label on every page pointing at it. A drafter cannot reword either without breaking the brief or the link. Commercial terms in prose are still caught everywhere, including in the body of 4.22.7 itself.

rules.description: Advice-pattern scan on Junior and Patient tiers
banned_phrases: you do not need to see a doctor
